Hot Joint or Bursa in an Adult

septic arthritis, crystal arthritis and septic bursitis · synovial fluid thresholds · prosthetic joint and gonococcal branches · post-injection flareIs joint motion preserved, and has the fluid been sampled before any treatment?

1Presentation2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Presentation
Bottom line
  • Aspirate before you treat: no exam finding excludes infection, and a septic joint can destroy cartilage within days
  • Passive motion picks the space: kept, with swelling over the bursa, is bursitis; pain with any passive motion and a diffuse effusion is the joint
  • Nothing goes in before the sample (no antibiotic, colchicine, glucocorticoid or repeat injection), unless the patient is septic: then antibiotics do not wait for the tap
What it is

A hot, swollen joint or bursa in an adult: infection, crystals, or a reaction to an injection

Sort by

Passive range of motion, then the fluid

Hands off

Shoulder pain without a hot joint: Shoulder Pain; noninflammatory fluid: Osteoarthritis; arthritis after diarrhea or urethritis: Low Back Pain in an Adult (reactive arthritis, also called Reiter syndrome)

2Urgent risks
Septic arthritisA hot, swollen joint that hurts with any passive motion; fever

If passive motion of the joint hurts, choose arthrocentesis, then IV antibiotics at once, without waiting for culture results (the ladder, rung 2).

3Differential
Hot joint or bursa, most tempting first
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
Septic arthritisDiabetes, inflammatory arthritis, a prosthesis, injection drug useHours to days; fluid over 50,000 white cells, over 75% neutrophils; usually Staphylococcus aureus
GoutMan; the first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra); alcohol, diureticsAn untreated early flare typically settles in 7 to 10 days; negatively birefringent urate needles
Pseudogout (calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystal deposition disease)Chondrocalcinosis on the radiographWeakly positively birefringent, rhomboid crystals
Septic bursitisRed, warm swelling over the olecranon or kneecap (housemaid's knee); leaning, kneeling or an abrasionJoint motion kept; fever often absent; bursal Gram stain or culture, usually Staphylococcus aureus
Noninfectious bursitisSwelling over the bursa, as in septic bursitisBursal Gram stain and culture negative
Prosthetic joint infectionA knee or hip replacement; painLower cut-offs: over 3,000 white cells, over 80% neutrophils
Disseminated gonococcal infectionSexually active; migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, pustulesFluid count lower and Gram stain often negative; NAAT (nucleic acid amplification test) of the cervix, urethra, pharynx, rectum
Post-injection flarePain within 24 hours of a glucocorticoid injectionSettles within 48 hours; infection worsens over days instead

FluidWhite cells/mm³

4Workup
The hot joint: start on the lowest rung not yet tried
RungDoMove on when
1Arthrocentesis through clean skin or with ultrasound, never through cellulitisAlways, first
2IV antibiotics once culture samples are taken: vancomycin; add a gram-negative drug (ceftriaxone, or an antipseudomonal agent with immunosuppression or injection drug use) when gram-negative infection is suspected or vancomycin is not working; in sickle cell disease add Salmonella coverage (asplenic patients also need coverage for encapsulated organisms)Purulent fluid or over 50,000; do not wait for culture
3Drain the joint: repeated aspiration, or arthroscopic or open washoutSeptic arthritis confirmed
Treatment by cause
CauseTreatment
Septic bursitisAspirate, then antibiotics against Staphylococcus aureus; drainage, and incision and drainage when antibiotics fail
Gout flare, infection excludedAn NSAID first, or colchicine as the next choice; a glucocorticoid third, but first in kidney failure; colchicine or a glucocorticoid in heart failure or cirrhosis Between flaresBetween flares, allopurinol or febuxostat comes first; probenecid suits only patients who underexcrete uric acid. Started without NSAID or colchicine cover, urate lowering can set off a flare.
PseudogoutAn NSAID, a glucocorticoid or colchicine
Disseminated gonococcal infectionIV ceftriaxone with oral doxycycline
Any suspected infectionNo glucocorticoid injection into a joint or a bursa

Pause point. The bait: a crystal on the slide, or a history of gout, ends the search. Crystals do not exclude infection, and a high count is treated as septic until culture.

Practice
  1. 54-year-old woman has 1 day of a hot, swollen, red right knee severe pain on passive range of motion obesity, hypertension and diabetes Radiograph: joint space narrowing T 38.5 °C · HR 102/min · no rash → Arthrocentesis → nothing on exam excludes infection, and diabetes and joint space narrowing are risk factors for it: aspirate before any treatment
  2. 47-year-old woman has 2 days of a hot, swollen left knee pain with any passive motion aspirate: 68,000 white cells/mm³, 85% neutrophils No crystals seen under polarized light T 38.6 °C · Gram stain pending → Septic arthritis → over 50,000 white cells with over 75% neutrophils and no crystals is septic arthritis: vancomycin after cultures, then drainage
  3. 55-year-old man woke with severe pain at the base of the big toe red, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint began after a steak dinner Aspirate: 12,000 white cells/mm³ T 37.6 °C · negatively birefringent needles → Gout → an inflammatory count with negatively birefringent needles is gout: an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug) or colchicine
  4. 47-year-old woman has 2 days of a hot, swollen right knee aspirate shows negatively birefringent needle crystals and 60,000 white cells/mm³ Gram stain shows no organisms T 38.2 °C · culture pending → Treat as septic → crystals do not exclude coexisting infection: over 50,000 white cells is treated as septic until culture says otherwise
  5. 72-year-old woman has 1 day of a hot, swollen right knee radiograph shows chondrocalcinosis aspirate: positively birefringent rhomboid crystals Gram stain shows no organisms T 37.8 °C · aspirate 18,000 white cells/mm³ → Pseudogout → positively birefringent rhomboids with chondrocalcinosis are calcium pyrophosphate crystals: pseudogout
  6. 68-year-old man has 3 weeks of right knee pain had a knee replacement 2 years ago aspirate: 3,200 white cells/mm³, 82% neutrophils No crystals seen T 37.4 °C · radiograph: no loosening seen → Prosthetic joint infection → around a prosthesis the 50,000 threshold does not apply: over 3,000 white cells with over 80% neutrophils is prosthetic joint infection
  7. 24-year-old woman has 4 days of joint pain moving from knee to wrist tenosynovitis over the wrist extensors a few pustules on the hands Sexually active, inconsistent condom use T 38.1 °C · no back pain or conjunctivitis → Disseminated gonococcal infection → migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis and pustules are disseminated gonococcal infection: NAAT and cultures of cervix, urethra, pharynx and rectum
  8. 47-year-old woman has a hot, swollen left knee and fever red, warm cellulitis over the front of the knee the joint must be sampled Diabetes, on metformin T 38.4 °C · pain with passive motion · knee effusion → Arthrocentesis straight through the cellulitis → a needle through cellulitis seeds the joint: aspirate through clean skin or under image guidance
  9. 60-year-old man with sickle cell disease has a hot, swollen left knee pain with any passive motion aspirate cloudy, cultures drawn Empiric antibiotics are being chosen T 38.7 °C · aspirate 90,000 white cells/mm³ → Add Salmonella to coverage → sickle cell disease adds Salmonella to the organisms to cover
  10. 70-year-old man has 2 days of a diffusely swollen right knee severe pain with any passive motion fever and chills No swelling localized over the kneecap T 38.8 °C · large knee effusion → Septic arthritis → pain with any passive motion and a diffuse effusion is the joint, not the bursa: aspirate the joint
  11. 52-year-old man has a red, hot, tender swelling over the kneecap fever since yesterday full, painless passive knee motion Kneels on concrete at work T 38.6 °C · no knee effusion → Septic prepatellar bursitis → preserved joint motion with swelling over the bursa is extraarticular: septic prepatellar bursitis, aspirate the bursa
  12. 45-year-old man, a floor installer, has 3 days of knee swelling boggy swelling over the kneecap, red and warm knee range of motion intact Serum uric acid not yet drawn T 37.4 °C · no knee effusion → Aspirate the bursal fluid → redness and warmth make infection plausible: aspirate the bursal fluid before presuming crystals or overuse
  13. 49-year-old man was diagnosed with septic prepatellar bursitis no improvement after 3 days of antibiotics swelling and redness unchanged Culture grew Staphylococcus aureus T 38.0 °C · knee motion still full → Incision and drainage of the bursa → failure to improve on antibiotics is the drainage gate: incision and drainage of the bursa
  14. 58-year-old woman has worsening right shoulder pain began 4 days after a subacromial corticosteroid injection fever and myalgias Pain was mild the day after the injection T 38.4 °C · white cells 14,000/mm³ → Image-guided aspiration of the bursa → pain worsening days after an injection is iatrogenic inoculation of skin flora: image-guided aspiration of the deep bursa
  15. 60-year-old man has severe right shoulder pain began 6 hours after a corticosteroid injection already easing by the next morning No chills or redness at the injection site Afebrile · white cells normal · no swelling → Post-injection steroid flare → pain within hours that settles within 48 hours is a post-injection steroid flare; infection worsens over days
Distractors Naproxen: skips a rung; treats a diagnosis not yet made and delays drainage. Serum uric acid: wrong parameter; neither rules gout in nor infection out.
Pairs with Septic Arthritis and Transient Synovitis in a Child: in adults every acute hot joint is aspirated at rung 1; only in children does rung 1 depend on toxicity and inflammatory signs, not on the presence of fluid.
Transferable rule

When a test is both diagnostic and therapeutic and the disease it excludes is time-destructive, the test comes before every treatment outside sepsis, even one right for the more likely diagnosis. Aspirate the space that may be infected, because infection cannot be excluded.
